Where this started

How four programs are built

  • From a $20 tote to a $290 one, three local programs build it the same way. SunLife Organics. Alfred Coffee. Erewhon.
  • A small set that never leaves the shelf, with limited runs on top. Newness lives in the drops, never in the core.
  • Our own range over the same period: 14 styles at Brentwood, 6 at Westlake. The second-best design was not carried at Westlake.
  • Have a Nice Day: 99 of 187 units across two builds, and the top seller at both shops.

Core 04 · Bags

Classic Tote Bag

$55
41 units · 3rd

Tan oversized canvas, NEIGHBORLY wordmark, Have a Nice Day tag. Cost $25.95.

Tote economics. Est. cost $25.95. At $55 the gross is $29.05, a 52.8% margin; at the earlier $35 it was $9.05, or 25.9%. Comparable totes: SunLife $20, Alfred $32, Erewhon $65. Hat costs are not yet confirmed.
Mark placement. NEIGHBORLY on the cap front, the place name stitched above the closure on the back. A new territory changes the back only.

What is costed. Only the Classic Tote has a quote: $25.95 against a $55 price, 47.2% of retail. The three hat costs above are modelled at that same ratio and need confirming against the actual buy. Gross at full sell-through is $9,824, a 52.8% margin. The Q1 drop cap is a separate 100-unit buy and is not priced yet.
Against last quarter. 10 Apr to 24 Jun sold 187 units across 7 styles, about $5,843 at retail and $2,757 at cost on the same ratio. The proposed buy is 2.1x those units and 3.2x that cost. Four of the seven old prices are actual register AURs; three are assumed.
